text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Europe is striving for a solution to the Cyprus problem before accession talks start.
- The state-run electricity authority is to decide within one month on the fate of tenders for the supply of turbines to a new station.
- The European Union "will pay for its criminal stance" over Cyprus, Greek Foreign Minister Theodoros Pangalos warns.
- Russia raises Turkish threats to settle the fenced-in town of Varosha at the United Nations.
- Cyprus Airways appoints a new chief pilot ahead of a Civil Aviation Authority deadline.
- Bad handling of Cyprus's entry negotiations to the European Union could be a boomerang, said Communist Akel general secretary Demetris Christofias.

- Nicosia remains reserved in its reactions to European insistence on including Turkish Cypriots in the negotiating procedure. House President Spyros Kyprianou discloses British envoy on Cyprus, Sir David Hannay, described the EU position as a warning to Cyprus.
- Greece will block enlargement of the EU if it insists on Turkish Cypriots inclusion in Cyprus' accession talks.
